survivors.title: Eink mid-verse merge mis-detects a displaced verse anchor and relocates a verse's first word into the prior verse (est 10:2 'Aren't' corrupted on the shipped flagship)
survivors.evidence: _merge_mid_verse_breaks treats ALL leading prose before a verse-p block's first verse marker as the prior verse's tail: `is_break = bool(_MV_PROSE_WORD_RE.search(lead)) and mk is not None and has_anchor` (5650), then `inners[prev_idx] = tail + glue + prefix; inners[i] = inner[mk.start():]` (5657-5658). But when a verse's anchor is DISPLACED past its own opening word(s) (the known-by-design v1/v2 anchor displacement, settled item #9 — here a mid-chapter instance), that leading prose is the CURRENT verse's head, not the prior verse's tail. Proven by running the real shipped function on a copy of epub_working/index_split_028.html: the base block for `v-est-10-2` opens `Aren’t ... 2all the acts of his power...`; the clean WEB source (content/translations/sources/web/eng-web_vpl.txt:12868-12869) shows EST 10:1 ends '...islands of the sea.' and EST 10:2 BEGINS 'Aren’t all the acts of his power...'. After `_merge_mid_verse_breaks` (returned merged_count=1): est 10:1 now ends '...islands of the sea. Aren’t ¹²' and est 10:2 now reads 'all the acts of his power...' — verse 2's first word silently moved to verse 1. I classified all 26 merge sites against clean WEB text: 25 are genuine prior-verse tails (correct), est 10:2 is the ONLY false-positive. Eink-only (call site 5700 is gated on resolve_target_reader=='eink'), so it corrupts the shipped Ethiopian eink flagship but not the byte-stable KJV editions. No gate catches it: G1 golden hash is KJV-only, there is no eink text-integrity golden gate, and dev/audit_verse_formatting.py endorses the merge (flags est 10:2 as a mid_verse_break ERROR via the same displacement-blind detector).
survivors.fix: Make the merge displacement-aware: before relocating `prefix`, confirm it is NOT a prefix of the CURRENT verse's canonical text. The clean text is co-located in the same base file as the verse's `vnote-<book>-<ch>-<v>` popup aside (vnote-est-10-2 = 'Aren’t all the acts of his power...'); if the stripped `lead` is a leading substring of that verse's vnote text, the anchor is merely displaced (not a calibre mid-verse split) — skip the merge (leaving a benign un-merged break is strictly safer than reordering scripture). This discriminator cleanly separates all 26 sites (only est 10:2's lead matches its current verse's head; every genuine lead matches the PRIOR verse's tail). Apply the same guard to dev/audit_verse_formatting.py so it stops reporting displaced anchors as mid_verse_break ERRORs. Add est 10:2 to a regression test (e.g. test_midverse_keepset_parity.py / a new test_midverse_displacement_guard) and extend a text-integrity golden gate to the eink flagship build so this scripture-corruption class cannot ship undetected (G1 currently covers only the 9 KJV editions).
survivors.verifierFix: Make the merge displacement-aware using the CANONICAL BASE TEXT (the WEB source that the scripture body is built from), NOT the popup aside (which is a different/KJV-style translation, as proven by vnote-est-10-2 = "And all the acts...", not "Aren't all the acts..."). Concretely, in _merge_mid_verse_breaks before the relocation at 5654: derive the alphabetic word-sequence of `lead`, and SKIP the merge (leave the benign un-merged break) when that word-sequence is a PREFIX of the CURRENT verse's canonical WEB text AND is NOT a SUFFIX of the PRIOR verse's canonical WEB text. The current/prior verse ids are already in hand (mk's anchor v-est-10-2 and the prior block's last v-anchor), and content/translations/sources/web/eng-web_vpl.txt (book-code-mapped est->EST) is the source of the base body, so it is the right oracle. I verified this discriminator separates all 26 sites: est 10:2 lead "Aren't" IS a prefix of WEB 10:2 "Aren't all the acts..." -> skip (fixes the bug); 1co 9:2 lead "Aren't you my work in the Lord?" is NOT a prefix of WEB 9:2 "If to others I am not an apostle..." (it is the tail of WEB 9:1) -> still merges; gen 48:2 lead "He took with him his two sons..." is NOT a prefix of WEB 48:2 "Someone told Jacob..." (it is the tail of WEB 48:1, which ends with terminal punctuation "...is sick.\"") -> still merges. Note the "prior verse ends in terminal punctuation" and "lead is short / starts with Aren't" shortcuts both FAIL (gen 48:2 and 1co 9:2 disprove them) -> the WEB-source comparison is the only reliable discriminator. Keep the eink gating so the 9 KJV editions remain byte-identical (additive, eink-only). Add a regression test pinning est 10:2 (must NOT merge) and 1co 9:2 (must STILL merge) as the counter-example. Mirror the same guard in dev/audit_verse_formatting.py so it stops reporting est 10:2 as a mid_verse_break ERROR. Extending a text-integrity golden gate to the eink flagship is desirable but secondary (the eink full build is currently OOM-blocked); the displacement guard + the est/1co regression test are the load-bearing fix.

survivors.title: The only real-build byte-stability gate checks determinism on 3 default-profile editions and never builds the tablet/kindle/everywhere KJV target variants — it cannot catch an eink-gating leak or a uniform re-baseline; G1 must build all 3x3 variants with stored goldens
survivors.evidence: The module docstring explicitly REJECTS golden hashes — "a stored golden hash would be fragile against the per-build URN; reproducibility is self-maintaining" (lines 16-18) — and the test only asserts rebuild==rebuild determinism (line 98 `assert _content_digest(rebuilt) == digests[rebuild_target]`). Consequences: (a) a code change that re-baselines all editions uniformly PASSES the determinism check (both builds carry the new hash); (b) the tablet and kindle VARIANTS of the 9-KJV set — which exercise the eink-OFF state of the `resolve_target_reader`/`eink=` branches differently from 'everywhere' (e.g. tablet's `resolve_note_popup_split_cap`->0 at line 3346, `apply_tablet_popup_strip_separators`) — are never built, so a leak into them is invisible; (c) eastern-orthodox is never byte-checked at all.

Supersede this determinism-only test (its anti-golden rationale is now wrong for the byte-stable set). This is what converts the Finding-1 isolation from 'correct today, unprovable' to 'gate-enforced'.
survivors.verifierFix: Add G1 = tests/test_kjv_golden_hash_gate.py + tests/golden/kjv_golden_hashes.json that builds the byte-stable KJV set across its target variants via apply_target_override/build_one's target_reader, normalizes ONLY the volatile OPF fields (URN, dcterms:modified, dc:date, rights-year — reuse _content_digest's regexes), and asserts each variant against a STORED hash. survivors.title: Build-output module core/eink_glyphs.py is missing from _PIPELINE_SCRIPTS, so editing its glyph table serves a STALE cached eink/kepub EPUB
survivors.evidence: _PIPELINE_SCRIPTS lists every build-output-shaping module (build_edition.py, matter_pages.py, core/edition_stats.py, core/covers.py, core/vnote_separators.py, ...) so a code edit busts the content-addressable cache key, but it OMITS core/eink_glyphs.py. That module is NOT data-mediated: scripts/core/eink_glyphs.py:17 holds a hardcoded table `EINK_CATEGORY_BADGE_GLYPHS = {"lang":"⌘", "text":"†", "comm":"◊", ...}` with no backing yaml/json. It IS baked into eink-target EPUB bytes at build time: build_edition.py:3303 imports `eink_category_badge_glyph`, used at :2860 (inline badge chips), :4042 (glossary cascade headers), :4330 (per-note badge glyph), and matter_pages.py:278 bakes it into the symbol-legend page. The module docstring itself says "Shared by scripts/build_edition.py (emitters) and scripts/matter_pages.py (the legend page) so the two can never drift." compute_cache_key hashes the whole edition record + notes + epub_working/ + the _PIPELINE_SCRIPTS allow-list, but never hashes eink_glyphs.py — so changing, say, `"comm":"◊"` to `"comm":"◆"` produces an identical cache key and `cache_lookup` returns the prior EPUB without rebuilding. is_output_current() is blind too (build_edition.py:6915 only `sources.extend(REPO_ROOT/'scripts'/s for s in _PS)`, so it inherits the same omission). This is the exact 'fix the class, not the instance' pattern round-5 closed for edition_stats (rated HIGH); eink_glyphs was added later (K-R13b, 2026-06-23) and slipped the net. Root cause for the silent miss: the guard tests/test_build_cache.py:323-355 only iterate the EXISTING _PIPELINE_SCRIPTS to prove each listed entry invalidates the key (test_key_changes_when_each_pipeline_script_changes) plus assert a hardcoded required subset is present — neither scans the orchestrators' imports for a build-path module that is MISSING from the list, so a newly-added baked-content module is never detected.
survivors.fix: Add `"core/eink_glyphs.py",` to _PIPELINE_SCRIPTS in scripts/core/build_cache.py (one fix point — this auto-covers both the content cache at part 9 and is_output_current's mtime list at build_edition.py:6915).
